title: Price-Per-Use Redemption Progress
dataSources: Micro-spend transactions (`microspend:txn`), no-spend days (`nospend:day`), price-per-use items (`priceperuse:item`), cash-back rewards (`cashback:reward`).
app: Bank-transaction exports categorised for micro-spending, no-spend-day trackers, price-per-use logs, and cash-back / rewards feeds — sent to Splunk HEC via scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=priceperuse:item
| eval cost_per_use=round(price/uses,2)
| stats latest(price) as price, latest(uses) as uses, latest(cost_per_use) as cost_per_use by item
| sort cost_per_use
description: Shows which purchases are earning their keep and which are still expensive clutter.
value: Price-per-use turns guilt about a purchase into an objective signal of whether it is becoming valuable over time.
implementation: Track item price and uses in `index=personal`; rank items by latest cost per use.
visualization: Table of items with price, uses, and current cost per use.
grandmaExplanation: It surfaces which purchases are finally earning their keep and which are still expensive things you barely touch.
